title: Photons and the photoelectric effect; Energy levels and spectra
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; Q01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; Q01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; Q02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: Q01-1#N.4b, Q02-1#N.6a, Q01-1#N.9a, Q02-1#N.13a, Q01-1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Continuous spectrum
items.clue: All wavelengths present, from a hot dense source such as a lamp filament.

items.label: Threshold frequency
items.clue: Symbol f₀: below it a metal emits no electrons, however intense the light.

items.label: Electronvolt
items.clue: Energy unit equal to 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, convenient for single quanta of light.

items.label: Emission line spectrum
items.clue: Bright features on a dark background, produced by a hot gas at low pressure.

questions.stem: Light with a wavelength of 500 nm in air passes from the air into water (n = 1.33). What is the energy of each photon while it travels through the water? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the speed of light in air as c.
An atom has only four energy levels: −1.50 eV, −2.50 eV, −4.00 eV and −6.00 eV. What is the energy of the emitted photon that has the SHORTEST wavelength?
questions.explanation: Largest gap: −1.50 eV → −6.00 eV, ΔE = 4.50 eV. Largest ΔE → highest f → shortest λ.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which observation from photoelectric experiments cannot be explained by the classical wave theory of light?

options.text: Photoelectrons are emitted without any measurable delay, even in very dim light.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the light is made much more intense.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the frequency of the light is raised.
Every photoelectron leaves the metal with kinetic energy exactly hf minus the work function.

questions.stem: An atom has energy levels at −10.0 eV (the ground state), −5.0 eV and −3.0 eV. An atom in its ground state is struck by a photon of energy 3.0 eV. What happens?

options.text: The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to the −3.0 eV energy level.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 15.0 or 13.0 eV.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 5.0 or 7.0 eV.
The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to an energy of −7.0 eV.

questions.stem: Light whose photons each have energy 4.0 eV shines on three metals: X, with work function 2.0 eV; Y, with work function 3.0 eV; and Z, with work function 4.5 eV. Which statement about the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from each metal is correct?

options.text: Z's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and X's electrons the least
X's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and Z emits no electrons
All three metals emit electrons, each with the same maximum kinetic energy
Their maximum kinetic energies cannot be ranked without the light's intensity
